children: Today at Groundbreak 2026, Procore Technologies, Inc. (

), the leading global provider of construction management software, launched Procore AI Go, a voice-first mobile app that lets construction crews ask questions and receive instant, spoken answers from their project data within Procore. Now available in open beta, the app helps reduce time spent manually searching through drawings and specifications so crews can stay focused on building.

To extend the voice experience hands-free, Procore is also partnering with Meta to bring Procore AI Go to AI glasses, giving construction crews a hands-free way to access project information and capture first-person photos by simply saying "Hey Procore,” without stopping work to reach for a phone. Together, these capabilities are part of Procore’s broader system of intelligence, helping teams see what’s happening in the field, understand it in context, and increasingly take action.

For contractors, every interruption on the jobsite comes at a cost. When crew leads have to stop work to track down drawings, confirm specifications, or document what happened in the field, productivity suffers and decisions can be delayed. A joint Procore and Dodge Construction report found contractors can recover two to six hours per person every week through deeper technology adoption. For contractors operating on tight margins and demanding schedules, that time adds up, creating an opportunity to spend less time on administrative work and more time building.

“Construction crews shouldn’t have to walk back to the trailer to find the information they need,” said Geoff Lewis, SVP of Product at Procore. “We’re bringing Procore AI directly to the people doing the work, giving them a faster way to get answers right where they are, in a hands free way. And as we explore technologies like AI glasses, we're looking at how to make it even easier for crews to access and capture information without putting down their tools.”
Bringing Procore AI to the Field

Procore AI Go connects to a customer’s project information in Procore, allowing field teams to ask questions through natural conversation and receive answers grounded in their project data. A field leader can ask about RFIs, submittals, drawings, specifications, or daily logs without stopping to navigate through screens. Because Procore AI Go understands the project context, it can surface the relevant information and supporting evidence and continue through natural follow-up questions.
Procore AI Go features:
Voice-powered answers –
Crews can ask questions about project drawings, specifications, RFIs, submittals, daily logs, observations, and inspections and receive spoken answers based on their information in Procore.
Push-to-talk controls –
Built for noisy jobsites, crews can activate Procore AI when they need it without surrounding conversations or jobsite noise triggering unintended interactions.
Conversation history –
Crews can return to previous conversations without starting over, with session history retained on their devices.
What's Next for Procore AI Go

Procore is developing additional capabilities that will allow field teams to take action directly from their phones. Soon, with Procore AI Go, crews will be able to create daily logs and observations, draft RFIs, and translate information through natural conversation and images, turning what they see and say in the field into structured project information while the context is still fresh.

Future updates will also bring Procore AI agents to the app. For example, the Daily Log Agent can help organize activity notes, photos, labor data, and site details and flag missing or conflicting information before a report is finalized. The Site Safety Agent can help teams identify and act on potential safety issues in the field like flagging a potential fall hazard for follow-up.

“Using Procore AI Go is like calling a teammate who knows the project inside and out,” said Andrew Baker, Chief Information Officer at Sequoyah Electric. “Our foremen can ask a question while they're looking at the problem and get an answer on the spot, without walking back to the trailer to search through drawings and specs. Our people have always picked up the phone to talk through issues with their team, so it feels familiar from day one, and it's simple and powerful enough that once they try it, they want to keep using it.”
Testing AI Glasses on Active Jobsites

Procore is partnering with Meta to bring Procore AI Go to AI glasses. The collaboration will explore how AI glasses could extend the Procore AI Go experience hands-free on active jobsites, allowing crews to capture first-person photos and access information about those images without stopping work to pull out a phone.

To better understand AI’s impact on field productivity, Procore is participating in a study with Moss Construction, independently designed by SBK Technologies1. The study will evaluate how AI agents, Procore AI Go, and AI-enabled wearables can reduce administrative tasks and give construction crews more time to focus on building.
Together, these capabilities advance Procore’s system of intelligence: helping teams see what’s happening in the field, understand it in context, and take action directly from where the work happens.
Availability

Procore AI Go is available today in open beta for customers in North America included across Procore’s Digital Coworker Starter, Pro, and Enterprise packages. The integration with Meta’s AI glasses is in closed beta.
To learn more, visit: www.procore.com/ai.
